phrases-7-40-camel-passing-through-the-e.title: Excluding the Arrogant 'Until the Camel Passes Through the Eye of the Needle'
phrases-7-40-camel-passing-through-the-e.note: Surah 7:40 declares that those who reject God's signs will not enter the Garden 'until the camel passes through the eye of the needle,' reproducing Jesus' proverb in Matthew 19:24 and Luke 18:25 alongside its Talmudic counterpart in Berakhot 55b.

discussion.view: Classical commentators explain this clause as a vivid Arabic proverb illustrating an impossibility, or as a shared truth spoken by earlier prophets.
discussion.reply: In the Synoptic Gospels (Matthew 19:24; Luke 18:25), Jesus coins the image of a camel passing through the eye of a needle regarding entry into the kingdom of God, while the Babylonian Talmud (Berakhot 55b) adapts it to an elephant; Surah 7:40 places the Gospel wording directly into divine speech.

phrases-7-40-camel-passing-through-the-e.quranEn: Surely those who call Our signs a lie, and are arrogant about it – the gates of the sky will not be opened for them, nor will they enter the Garden, until the camel passes through the eye of the needle. In this way We repay the sinners.
quranHighlights: nor will they enter the Garden, until the camel passes through the eye of the needle.

stories-7-11-18-iblis-refuses-to-bow-to-.title: Iblis Refusing to Prostrate to Adam Because Fire Surpasses Clay
stories-7-11-18-iblis-refuses-to-bow-to-.note: Surah 7:11–18 narrates God commanding the angels to prostrate before Adam and Iblis refusing because he was created from fire whereas Adam was created from clay, matching the Latin Vita Adae et Evae 13–16 and the Syriac Cave of Treasures.

discussion.view: Muslim commentators present the command for the angels to bow to Adam and Iblis's boast of fiery origin over clay as the primeval account of Satan's fall at the dawn of creation.
discussion.reply: Genesis 1–3 contains no command for angels to bow to Adam and no dialogue with Satan about fire and clay. The narrative of God commanding the angels to worship the newly formed Adam comes from the apocryphal Life of Adam and Eve (Vita Adae et Evae 13–16), and Satan's specific boast that he is 'fire and spirit' refusing to bow to 'a thing of dust' appears in the Syriac Cave of Treasures.

stories-7-11-18-iblis-refuses-to-bow-to-.quranEn: [11] Certainly We created you, (and) then fashioned you. Then We said to the angels, ‘Prostrate yourselves before Adam,’ and they prostrated themselves, except Iblīs. He was not one of those who prostrated themselves. [12] He said, ‘What kept you from prostrating yourself when I commanded you?’ He said, ‘I am better than him. You created me from fire, but You created him from clay.’ [13] He said, ‘Go down from here! It is not for you to be arrogant here. Get out! Surely you are one of the disgraced.’ [14] He said, ‘Spare me until the Day when they are raised up.’ [15] He said, ‘Surely you are one of the spared.’ [16] He said, ‘Because you have made me err, I shall indeed sit (in wait) for them (on) Your straight path. [17] Then I shall indeed come upon them, from before them and from behind them, and from their right and from their left, and You will not find most of them thankful.’ [18] He said, ‘Get out of here, detested (and) rejected! Whoever of them follows you – I shall indeed fill Gehenna with you – all (of you)!’
quranHighlights: We said to the angels, ‘Prostrate yourselves before Adam,’ and they prostrated themselves, except Iblīs.

stories-7-171-mount-sinai-shaken-above-i.title: God Suspending Mount Sinai Above Israel Like an Overhanging Canopy (Zullah)
stories-7-171-mount-sinai-shaken-above-i.note: Surah 7:171 states that God shook Mount Sinai above the Israelites as if it were an overhanging canopy (`zullah`) so that they thought it would fall upon them, matching the Talmudic aggadah of Sinai overturned above Israel like a tub in Shabbat 88a.

discussion.view: Traditional commentators such as al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir write that angels physically uprooted Mount Sinai and held it suspended over the heads of the Israelites until they accepted the covenant.
discussion.reply: In Exodus 19:17, the Hebrew phrase `be-tachtit ha-har` means 'at the foot of the mountain,' describing Israel standing at the base of Sinai. In Talmud Bavli Shabbat 88a and Avodah Zarah 2b, third-century amora Rav Avdimi bar Hama homiletically renders `tachtit` as 'beneath' to picture the mountain held overhead like an upturned cask (`gigit`).

stories-7-171-mount-sinai-shaken-above-i.quranEn: (Remember) when We shook the mountain above them, as if it were a canopy, and they thought it was going to fall on them: ‘Hold fast what We have given you, and remember what is in it, so that you may guard (yourselves).’
quranHighlights: We shook the mountain above them, as if it were a canopy, and they thought it was going to fall on them
‘Hold fast what We have given you

phrases-7-44-50-companions-of-the-fire-b.title: Calling Across the Partition: 'Pour Some Water on Us' From the Garden
phrases-7-44-50-companions-of-the-fire-b.note: In Surah 7:44–50, the companions of the Fire call across a partition (ḥijāb) to the companions of the Garden, 'Pour some water on us,' and are told it is forbidden, mirroring the Rich Man begging Abraham across the chasm for water in Luke 16:22–26.

discussion.view: Traditional commentators view this dialogue across the partition as a prophetic depiction of the Hereafter confirming truths taught by earlier messengers.
discussion.reply: The structural elements in Surah 7:44–50—the damned recognizing the blessed across an impassable barrier, crying out for water to cool their torment in the flame, and receiving a refusal—follow the narrative sequence of Jesus' parable of the Rich Man and Lazarus in Luke 16:22–26.

phrases-7-44-50-companions-of-the-fire-b.quranEn: [44] The companions of the Garden will call out to the companions of the Fire: ‘We have found what our Lord promised us (to be) true. So have you found what your Lord promised (to be) true?’ They will say, ‘Yes!’ And then a caller will call out among them: ‘The curse of God is on the evildoers, [45] who keep (people) from the way of God and desire (to make) it crooked, and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter.’ [46] Between both (groups) of them (there is) a partition, and on the heights (there are) men who recognize each (of them) by their marks, and they call out to the companions of the Garden: ‘Peace (be) upon you! They have not entered it, as much as they were eager (to do so).’ [47] And when their sight is turned toward the companions of the Fire, they say, ‘Our Lord, do not place us among the people who are evildoers.’ [48] The men of the heights will call out to men whom they recognize by their marks, (and) say, ‘Your hoarding is of no use to you, nor what you were arrogant (about). practices-7-31-32-take-your-adornment-at.title: Outlawing Pre-Islamic Naked Tawaf: 'Take Your Adornment at Every Mosque'
practices-7-31-32-take-your-adornment-at.note: Surah 7:31–32 commands 'Sons of Adam, take your adornment in every mosque,' abolishing the pre-Islamic Hums custom requiring non-Qurayshi pilgrims to circumambulate the Kaaba naked unless lent Hums garments.

discussion.view: Muslim exegetes explain that pagan Quraysh forced outside tribes to either rent Hums clothing or circle the Kaaba naked, and that Surah 7:31 restored modest dress to the Abrahamic sanctuary.
discussion.reply: Sahih Muslim 3028 and 1219 and Tafsir al-Tabari on 7:31 preserve the pre-Islamic ritual poetry recited by naked pilgrims circling the Meccan sanctuary. While ending the nudity taboo, Islamic pilgrimage law retained the underlying Meccan circumambulation (tawaf) and the requirement to shed ordinary stitched clothing for special sanctuary garments.

practices-7-31-32-take-your-adornment-at.quranEn: [31] Sons of Adam! Take your adornment in every mosque, and eat and drink, but do not act wantonly. Surely He does not love the wanton. [32] Say: ‘Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has brought forth for His servants, and the good things of (His) provision?’ Say: ‘It is exclusively for those who have believed in this present life on the Day of Resurrection.’ In this way We make the signs distinct for a people who know.
quranHighlights: Sons of Adam! Take your adornment in every mosque
Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has brought forth for His servants
